## https://kaidoplan.cygnusyang.top/features/resources.html

Features · 2 tools

# Resources

A plan that says three days is making an assumption about who is doing the work. Resources make the assumption explicit.

Updated 2026-11-16 · by cygnus, the developer of KaidoPlan

## The tools

Tool

Does

`resource_add`

Adds a person, piece of equipment or material. `units` and `efficiency` take part in effort conversion.

`resource_list`

Lists the project's resources.

## Why bother on a solo project

Because effort and duration are not the same number. Eight hours of work is one day for one person at full attention, two days at half, and four days if the "person" is also doing support that week. Recording the resource is how the plan carries that assumption instead of hiding it in an estimate.

On an AI-assisted project the resource model also covers the non-human parts: the CI runner that can only do one build at a time, the device that has to be free for a test. Those constraints behave exactly like a busy person.

## What it does not do

Do not read this as full resource-levelled scheduling with automatic reallocation. Resources inform effort conversion and appear on the plan; the scheduler's job here is the dependency graph and the dates.

## In practice

- Add the people who will actually do the work, with realistic units.

- Record shared equipment when it is a real bottleneck.

- Re-check the critical path after a resource change: a task that becomes half-time can move the end date without any dependency changing.

## Questions this page does not answer

Can I assign a task to a resource?

Tasks carry an `assignee`, which is the owner. Resources are the pool the plan describes; the two are related but not the same field.

Does efficiency affect dates?

It takes part in effort conversion, which is how duration is derived from effort — so yes, indirectly.

## https://kaidoplan.cygnusyang.top/features/baselines.html

Features · 5 tools

# Baselines and variance

Without a frozen schedule, it slipped is an opinion. A baseline turns it into two numbers.

Updated 2026-11-16 · by cygnus, the developer of KaidoPlan

## The tools

Tool

Does

`baseline_create`

Takes an immutable snapshot: planned start and finish plus completion state are frozen. Returns the baseline's id, name, colour and entry count.

`baseline_list`

Lists baselines in creation order, oldest first.

`baseline_variance`

Compares both the current plan and the actual dates against a baseline. Omitting the id uses the most recent one.

`baseline_delete`

Removes one baseline; the tasks are untouched.

`baseline_set_color`

Changes the palette colour of a baseline. Only the colour — the snapshot entries and creation time do not move.

## Two comparisons, not one

Planned-versus-baseline tells you the schedule changed. Actual-versus-baseline tells you the work took longer than promised. They are different facts and they lead to different conversations: the first is usually a scope or dependency decision, the second is an estimate problem.

`kaidoplan baseline create --file plan.kaido
kaidoplan baseline variance --file plan.kaido`

## When to take one

- At the start of each reporting period, so the report has a reference point.

- Before a delivery push, so the promise has a frozen state behind it.

- Before a large re-plan, so the cost of the re-plan is measurable afterwards.

## Immutability is the feature

A snapshot you can edit is a rumour. These entries are frozen at creation, which is why a baseline from three weeks ago still means what it meant then.

## Questions this page does not answer

Can I recover an old plan from a baseline?

A baseline records the planned dates at that moment; it is a reference, not a backup. Use the repository or your backup for restoration.

How many baselines can I keep?

They are cheap and listed in creation order. Keep the ones whose comparison you would actually make.

## https://kaidoplan.cygnusyang.top/features/cli.html

Features · CLI

# The command line

Everything the app can do to the plan, from a terminal — which is also the shortest path to putting a schedule check in CI.

Updated 2026-11-16 · by cygnus, the developer of KaidoPlan

## The command surface

`kaidoplan project create|open|save|summary
kaidoplan task add|list|get|update|delete
kaidoplan wbs import
kaidoplan schedule compute|path
kaidoplan violations
kaidoplan status update|batch
kaidoplan resource add|list
kaidoplan baseline create|list|delete|color|variance`

Every command takes `--file`; JSON output is available where a script needs structure rather than formatted text. The CLI works whether or not the app is open — it opens the file, performs the operation and saves.

## The four commands worth memorising

`kaidoplan schedule compute --file plan.kaido # dates from the graph
kaidoplan schedule path --file plan.kaido # the chain that sets the date
kaidoplan violations --file plan.kaido # what the plan admits is broken
kaidoplan status batch --file plan.kaido # write progress back, per-entry`

## Why a CLI and not only an MCP server

The MCP server needs the app and a client. A shell command needs neither, which makes it the option that survives in scripts, in CI and in a shell history you can read six months later. The two surfaces are the same operations on the same file, so choosing one is not choosing a different feature set.

## Putting it in CI

A dependency cycle can be made a build failure in one line. That is a cheap guarantee: it means no commit can introduce a plan that can never start, and it costs nothing when the check passes.

## Questions this page does not answer

Does the CLI need a licence?

You can use these commands during the free trial. CLI and MCP write operations require an active subscription after the trial.

Can I use it without the app installed?

The CLI is a separate Homebrew package. Whether it needs the app's licence state depends on the operation — reads do not.

## https://kaidoplan.cygnusyang.top/features/mcp-clients.html

Features · Integration

# Connecting an agent

Five clients, one switch each. The configuration file keeps its formatting, its key order and its other servers.

Updated 2026-11-16 · by cygnus, the developer of KaidoPlan

## What the switch does

Turning on a client writes its MCP configuration for you: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and WorkBuddy each have a row with a switch. Turning it off removes the same entry. The editor is text-preserving — it adds or removes only `mcpServers.kaidoplan` (for Codex, `[mcp_servers.kaidoplan]`), so indentation, key order and line endings in the rest of the file are untouched.

Each row reports its own state: connected, configuration needs updating, write failed with a reason and a retry, not connected, client not installed. A failure in one client does not affect the others.

## Stdio without a separate install

The app binary can run as a stdio MCP server with `--mcp-stdio`. That mode is intercepted very early in launch: no window, no Dock icon, nothing to close. A client can therefore start the app itself rather than depending on a separately installed CLI.

## The security defaults

- Loopback only — never the LAN, never the internet.

- A bearer token generated locally must accompany every request; it is shown in the panel and can be reset.

- Only folders authorized in the panel are reachable.

- Since v3.4.0 the service is on by default on `127.0.0.1`; an existing explicit off setting is respected rather than overwritten.

## Ports

The first successful bind is persisted, so restarts prefer the same port. If it is taken, the app falls back through a private range of 56 ports without changing the stored preference — so the next launch still tries your port first.

## Try reading and updating a plan

The trial includes both read and write access. After the trial, write-back requires a subscription. The service checks the licence before writing to disk.

## Questions this page does not answer

Do I have to use the switch?

No. A copy-configuration button remains as the manual path for anyone who wants to place the entry themselves.

What happens when the token changes?

Configurations of enabled clients are rewritten automatically, so you do not have to re-paste them.
